topics.name: Topic 1 Applied anatomy and physiology
points: 1.1.1 to 1.1.3 Functions of the skeleton, classification of bones and named bones
1.1.4 to 1.1.5 Classification of joints and joint movements in sporting skills
1.1.6 Ligaments and tendons
1.1.7 to 1.1.8 Muscle types and named voluntary muscles and their functions
1.1.9 Antagonistic (agonist and antagonist) muscle pairs
1.1.10 Fast and slow twitch muscle fibre types
1.1.11 Skeletal and muscular systems working together
1.2.1 to 1.2.2 Functions of the cardiovascular system; structure of the heart and valves
1.2.3 Arteries, capillaries and veins; blood pressure
1.2.4 Vasoconstriction, vasodilation and vascular shunting
1.2.5 Components of blood: red and white blood cells, platelets and plasma
1.2.6 to 1.2.7 Composition of inhaled and exhaled air; vital capacity and tidal volume
1.2.8 to 1.2.9 Components of the respiratory system; alveoli and gaseous exchange
1.2.10 Cardiovascular and respiratory systems working together
1.3 Aerobic and anaerobic exercise: energy release, lactic acid; fats and carbohydrates as fuels
1.4 Short-term effects of exercise on lactate, heart rate, stroke volume, cardiac output and breathing
1.4.6 Interpreting graphs of heart rate, stroke volume and cardiac output

topics.name: Topic 2 Movement analysis
points: 2.1.1 First, second and third class levers
2.1.2 Mechanical advantage and disadvantage
2.2 Planes and axes of movement: sagittal/frontal axis, frontal/sagittal axis, transverse/vertical axis

topics.name: Topic 3 Physical training
points: 3.1 Relationship between health, fitness and exercise
3.2.1 Components of fitness and their relative importance in sport
3.2.2 to 3.2.4 Fitness tests: purpose, protocols, selection and tests for each component
3.2.3 Collecting and interpreting fitness test data against normative tables
3.3.1 Principles of training, FITT, thresholds of training and heart rate zone calculations
3.3.2 Factors in choosing training methods and intensities
3.3.3 Training methods and fitness classes: advantages and disadvantages
3.4 Long-term effects of aerobic and anaerobic training: musculoskeletal and cardio-respiratory adaptations
3.5.1 to 3.5.2 PARQ and injury prevention
3.5.3 to 3.5.4 Common sporting injuries and RICE
3.5.5 Performance-enhancing drugs
3.6 Warm up and cool down: purpose, phases and activities

topics.name: Topic 4 Use of data (assessed in Components 1 and 2)
points: 4.1.1 to 4.1.2 Data analysis in sport; qualitative and quantitative data collection
4.1.3 Presenting data in tables and graphs
4.1.4 to 4.1.5 Interpreting, analysing and evaluating data, including against normative data

topics.name: Topic 1 Health, fitness and well-being
points: 1.1.1 to 1.1.3 Physical, emotional and social health benefits of participation
1.1.4 Positive and negative health effects of fitness
1.1.5 Designing and evaluating a personal exercise programme

1.3.4 to 1.3.5 Factors affecting optimum weight and optimum weight by sporting role
1.3.6 to 1.3.7 Energy balance and hydration

topics.name: Topic 2 Sport psychology
points: 2.1.1 Classification of skills on continua: open/closed, basic/complex, organisation
2.1.2 to 2.1.3 Practice structures and selecting practice to develop skills

2.3.1 to 2.3.2 Types of guidance: advantages, disadvantages and suitability

points: 3.1 Engagement patterns: participation factors (gender, age, socio-economic group, ethnicity, disability) and trend data

topics.name: Component 3 Practical Performance
points: Practical performance in three activities (one team, one individual, one free choice): skills in isolation and in competitive situations

points: Six to eight week PEP: aim and planning analysis
Carrying out and monitoring the PEP
Evaluating the PEP
